 ArchForge 

 Why is your use case a strong fit for WebMCP? 

 Architecture design is iterative and structured. WebMCP lets an agent safely
create, change, validate, and export the same living architecture model a
person sees, instead of returning disconnected chat output. 

 How does it create a better user experience? 

 People and agents work on one inspectable architecture. The human provides
context and makes final choices; the agent makes structured changes and
analysis. Recommendations explain rationale and tradeoffs, while Signals shows
every agent action and result. 

 What can people and agents do together that was difficult or impossible before? 

 Together, they can turn requirements and constraints into a provider-neutral
architecture, evaluate AWS or Azure options, identify risks, and export a
validated design—all while keeping decisions visible, editable, and reversible. 

 How did you implement WebMCP? 

 ArchForge detects document.modelContext and registers typed, runtime-validated
WebMCP tools over its application services. UI and agent actions share the same
command path; tools return structured results, mutation details, and safe
errors. The design_system workflow validates requests before making changes
and reports each step.
